title: Titrations, Concentrations and the Mole
opener_concept: Counting coins by weighing a sealed money bag (mass / mass-of-one = number), then sharing them into jars (amount / volume = concentration): the exact two moves of moles and concentration.
notes: All 15 bank problems (bronze 6, silver 5, gold 4) fresh-solved from display; every stored answer and unit was already correct, so no answer/number was changed. Added guided_steps to all 15 (unit-conversion box made explicit wherever cm3 was given; phase:substitute boundary set after the set-up/known-moles; every walk ends with a divide-back check stating the answer WITH unit). Added a plain-text hint to every problem (gold had neither hint nor equation_hint before, which would have failed the validator); kept all existing equation_hint fields byte-for-byte. Rebuilt each misconception with a derived expect committed from a real error (unit slip, inverse, wrong Mr, ignored/mis-read mole ratio, wrong titration volume, un-scaled aliquot); all sit outside the accept window and none equal the correct answer. Added tier_guides (bronze/silver/gold) with worked examples, tier descriptions, guided.opener, and three guided.teach walks (problems NOT in the bank). Slimmed method_card to 3 short paragraphs under budget. Board-neutral throughout: no board named, no equation-sheet claims; teach.bronze uses 'check whether your board gives you this equation'. Scrubbed inherited em dashes from exam_context.frequency and worked_examples step labels (colon) to pass the hard style gate. No circuit/chart figures: this is a pure-formula titration lesson, so figures_added is empty per spec. Tier ladder already matched bronze=one-step / silver=titration+ratio / gold=multi-step; no reordering needed. Propagation: all_row_ids contained only the canonical row; patched it; verified live == shard byte-for-byte and validator PASS on live. Note: the shared scratchpad file _live_canonical.json was clobbered mid-task by a parallel session, so this build fetched and used a fingerprint-unique live file (_L03_b360_live.json).
